properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/15/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in West Bethlehem Township, Washington county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/15/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8165818
Permit API: 125-23126
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: West Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/15/2023
Comments: On 11/15/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Cowden 55 well. On 08/23/2023, a routine partial inspection was conducted (IR 3606258).On 08/23/2023, the tank onsite displayed oil which looked as thought it was dripping down the side fro the top. The oil was on a small section of gravel. A smaller section of oil was on another side of the tank. The operator was notified the day of observation. There were no violations issued on 08/23/2023 due to size of area impacted. During inspection on 11/15/2023, for following was observed: The site appeared remediated regarding the oil from the top of the tank; the operator removed the impacted gravel and placed it in a bucket marked with 08/24/2023. The bucket remianed onsite; I recommend that this is removed and disposed of a an approproate waste facility (Photos 1-4). It also looked as thought the operator had wiped the side of the tank off. During the followup, a conductivity test was performed underneath the lower valve on the tank, which displayed iron stained gravel. Conductivity readings within the iron stained gravel, under the valve, yielded elevated results (Photos 5-7).During the initial inspection, a gas odor was noticed near the wellhead and I informed the operator. They informed operation's to inspect. They informed me that the grey apparatus on the well (Photo 8) was part of the landowner's hookup. When the operator followed up, their gas meter did not detect any gas. During the 11/15/23 follow up, the odor was noticed again to which I informed the operator. They followed up the same day and mentioned that the heater on the landowner's setup was functioning properly and may be bleeding; they recommendded a pressure test be performed. I contacted the landowner to inform them of what Diversified (operator) informed me of - they also contacted the landowner. I contacted the landowner about my conversation with the operator and recommended that the setup receives maintenance. The operator informed me that they thought the odor contained mercaptan and may be coming from a Columbia gas line nearby. Below the wellsite is a Williams station that the gas flows to. Regarding the elevated conductivity observed onsite below the valve of the production tank, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-10-21 to Jklm Energy Llc in Pike Twp, Potter county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Jklm Energy Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-10-21
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 865782
Permit API: 105-21919
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Pike Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-10-21
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the JKLM - Judson Hollow 302 Well Pad located in Pike Twp, Potter Co. on 10/21/2019 @1240 hours. The weather was 68 degrees and sunny. Profrac and JKLM were onsite performing stimulation activities on the 3HU well. During the course of the inspection, fluid was observed along northern edge of pad-wide containment. The fluid on the pad surface had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. The working tanks along the northern edge were in their own secondary containment. This containment had fluid with a field conductivity of 1200uS/cm. The working tank secondary containment was sitting within the pad-wide containment. This pad-wide containment was holding fluid with a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. The fluid level appeared to be above the rig matting. Upon closer inspection with JKLM personnel, a hole/tear was discovered in the corner of pad-wide containment approximately half way down, releasing the fluid to the pad surface. Sample 4427-193 was collected from the "Over Range" fluid on the pad surface. JKLM immediately propped up the tank containment to allow vac truck hoses to begin removing the fluid from the pad-wide containment where the tear was located. The area where the fluid was visible on the pad surface was cordoned off to keep traffic from tracking the fluid onto other areas of the well pad. The Operator also contacted the containment company to initiate repair. I received email confirmation from the Operator that as of 1800 hours the spill had been remediated. The email states, "Once puddles were recovered, soil in the impacted area was screened for specific conductance on a 12'x12' grid (see pre-excavation screening drawing). Damp pad material was then removed to a depth of between 1-2" and placed in a 20 yd. dumpster (OT 048). Post-excavation soil screening readings were then obtained (the highest reading was 1.23 mS/cm). The cleanup was complete by 1800 hrs." Violations of the following regulations are cited against the 3HU well, API#105-21922, as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED. CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)

Comments: On May 20 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the CFR USX 5 OG Well in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4157445.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed the water flowing onto the access road. It did not appear any remedial actions have been taken to address the flowing water and resulting erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road.The water was observed flowing down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water. The water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. Comments: On August 19, 2024 the Department (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of State Game Lands 51B1 Well located in Dunbar Township, Fayette County, where violations were continued for a release from production equipment inside the green shed.At the time of this inspection, Minor rutting is developing in the access road as it enters the well site; therefore, the Department recommends the operator continue to monitor and maintain the access road as necessary in order to prevent any erosion and sedimentation events from occurring. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniformand adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the area where a production tank had previously been placed. The DEP recommends this area be seeded and mulched. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.Two production tanks within secondary containment were observed. One of the production tanks appeared rusted but no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed. However, the tank's secondary containment was nearly full of fluid. The DEP recommends that the containment be drained, fluid be disposed of properly, and in accordance with regulations. The well tag was present at the time of this inspection. A well tag was found on the ground near wellhead. The Dept recommends the Operator permanently affix the well tag in accordance with 3211(h) . There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. No fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank near the wellhead onsite, however, the production tanks lid was cracked in half and open and there appeared to be a high level of fluid in this production tank. The DEP recommends the Operator replace the lid on this production tank and properly dispose of the contents within this tank to prevent a potential release. The production tank near the green shed had a hose inside the secondary containment extending out onto the ground. It appears that water in the secondary containment is being discharged to the ground as the secondary containment is at capacity. The Department recommends the removal of this excess fluid in accordance with current regulations to accommodate any potential releases that may occur. Inside the green shed located on this well site, a compressor station as well as various barrels with various unknown substances not in containment were observed. Some barrels were heavily rusted and staining in the gravel was observed underneath them as well as under the GPU and production equipment. The Department request the Operator provide information on what exactly is in the drums and what they are being used for. The Department request that this information be provided with the NOV response. The Department also recommends that the Operator remove all equipment/supplies not necessary for production.Inside the green shed, the spill that was previously observed in inspection reports 3743832 and 3808945 remains. In this green shed, the spill appears to be an oily like petroleum substance on the ground. The DEP again recommends that the Operator remediate the areas as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The DEP again requests the operator evaluate the releases that have occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. The GPU unit (not in secondary containment) in this green shed had no observable active leaks or discharge.Based on today's inspection violations for the spill shall remain outstanding along with failure to have the well tag permanently affixed to the wellhead.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 873437
Permit API: 015-23413
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-01-10
Comments: On January 10, 2020, Department representative John Ciccone conducted an investigation in response to a reported spill at Chief's SGL-36 pad. Kellon Balum (Chief Oil & Gas) notified Phone Duty Officer (Andrew Hobbins) that on January 9, 2020 at 0900 hours, of a spill of approximately 1-2 barrels of a production fluid/freshwater mixture to soil at the SGL-36 Pad in Overton Township, Bradford County. The department arrived onsite at 1000 hours and met with Kellon Balum and Brendan Logan of Chief Oil and Gas. The site was busy with tankers driving onto / off of the pad. During a pressure test, a 2 inch hole was discovered in a saddle unit. Before the hole could be fixed, a check valve failed which resulted in the spill of a mixture of production fluids and freshwater. Since the incident has been reported, the gate valve and check valve have been replaced in order to ensure subsequent failures do not happen. The site of the spill (photo #1) has been excavated by contractor Thompson. The excavation was being overseen by Brendan Logan of Chief. The excavated pit was dug out down to bedrock. No standing water was noted within the pit during the time of the inspection. Dug out soil was placed within 2 waste management (WM) containers (photo #2). 1 WM container will be shipped out to Waste Management today, and the other will remain onsite within its secondary containment for possible future use. Chief was in process of extending the excavated pit in order to ensure thorough removal of impacted soils during the time of the inspection. Site was departed at 1040 hours. The release of production fluids on the well pad is in violation of CSL 402(b), 78a.57, and SWMA 301. This release has been referred to Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields due to the quantity reported. Violations cited.

Comments: On November 29, 2023, DEP representatives Brad Kline, Erica Lutz, and Evan Buck conducted an follow up inspection at the Range Resources Cornwall Mountain 1-8H. This is to follow up with a reported spill by Range Resources on the afternoon of November 25, 2023 of approximately a barrel of production fluid. The production fluid was noticed bubbling from the well pad surface in the area of the buried dump line for the GPUs. Range Resources found a small hole in the the buried dump line from the GPU to the production fluid tanks during the initial excavation where the bubbling was occurring.Range Resources was continuing to excavate near and around the buried GPU dump line. The excavation area at the time of inspection was about 70 feet by 6 feet with a depth of approximately 5 feet. Range Resources was continually measuring the soil conductivity of the the area around the dump line. The soil conductivity in that area was approximately 3,000 uS/cm. Impacted soil was being placed on containment to be staged until a dump truck could be onsite to take the soil to the landfill. Kirby Steck with Range Resources said they plan to continue excavation along the dump line until lower soil conductivity levels are found.No new violations noted. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3650079.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/22/2026 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Liberty Township, Tioga county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/22/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8278991
Permit API: 117-22299
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/22/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that an estimated 5 gallons of produced fluid was released through a hole in a section of secondary containment. It rained heavily during this inspection. Six wells have been drilled and stimulated on the well pad. It appears that flowback operations are complete. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition.A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment near the production tanks. The tanks and secondary containment appear to be in good condition. No holes or patches were observed in the containment liner. The containment appeared to be retaining water. The fluid within the containment had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 947 uS/cm. The puddles on the pad surface near the containment had an EC of less than 900 uS/cm. A bucket within the secondary containment had a label on it which says spill waste for disposal. In one corner of the containment, the fluid in the containment had a petroleum sheen on it. A water truck driver arrived during this inspection and began to vacuum out the containment during this inspection. In a phone call with Brett Staller of Repsol, he stated that a water truck driver had dropped a hose on the secondary containment liner for the frac tank battery and created a 4-6 inch hole in the containment. Pad material was excavated beneath the hole and the hole was patched, he stated. I could not see a hole or patch in the liner during this inspection but there was approximately 2 inches of stormwater in the containment at the time due to the heavy rain. The bottom of the liner was also obscured where a petroleum sheen was present on the surface of the stormwater in the southeast corner of the containment. Violations cited and are considered immediately corrected.

I was accompanied by Paul Stiner of Diversified, Albatros representative, and remediation personal. Adjacent to the tanks, the F23 well was being swabbed. A sump was dug and fluids vacced out. Tanks 1 and 2 to be removed.Some elevated conductivity readings within the water were noted within the sump behind tank 3 and nearby (Photos 1-6).A sheen was seen within the water behind tank 4; this sheen appeared to be a combination of biological material and production fluid. I recommend to ensure liner does not continue to fall (Photo 20).A dozer was onsite to correct the access road leading to additional wells on the property (Photo 22). Rig onsite for swabbing of F23 (Photo 23).Manure around site yields high readings, however this is common. A comparible reading was taken at a low spot at the base of the earthern berm and it displayed an acceptable reading of 1.80 mS. This well in in a horse pasture (Photos 24, 25).Due to current remediation measures, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being noted and immediately corrected. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further inspection.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's (Blackhill) Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/10/2023 at 1525 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted to evaluate remedial activities that were conducted after a release that occurred on 4/6/2023.Moody and Associates Inc. (Moody's)(Environmental consultant) was onsite during my inspection and have been conducting field screenings for Blackhill. Since the release that occurred on 4/6/2023, Blackhill has had the entire southern stormwater conveyance channel excavated (photos #2, 3 and 4). Blackhill reported that soil readings in the channel were now field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Excavation points on both sides of the access road culvert are now acting as sumps for the collection of residual fluids. A water truck was stationed at these points today, recovering any collected fluids. The pad surface area that was determined to be impacted by the release has been excavated as much as possible (photos #6 and 7). Blackhill explained that collected fluids shown in photo #7 are also being recovered. Fluid in this area, which is located right next to the initial release point, was field measured at ~17.8mS/cm today. Blackhill reported that equipment will be brought in on either 4/11/2023 or 4/12/2023 to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure in order to excavate beneath them. The impacted stormwater basin has been emptied to where just a few puddles remain (photo #1). All water collected from the basin was stored in tanks shown in photo #9 and continues to be trucked offsite for disposal or reuse. I field measured a small puddle near the stormwater channel entry point of the basin which returned a reading of ~1.75mS/cm. All impacted materials that have been recovered are stored in lined and covered waste containers which are held on secondary containment (photo #8). All violations associated with the releases from 1/2/2023 and from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1620 hours.As a follow-up to the violations cited on 4/6/2023, the DEP requests a summary of the quantity of fluids collected in regards to the produced water release, including the stormwater basin, and where the water was transported after collection. This information can be provided in the NOV response.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-26
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 863613
Permit API: 081-21656
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Eldred Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-26
Comments: On September 26, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline conducted an incident investigation at Inflection Energy Winter Well Pad. The Department received notice that Inflection was planning on plugging the conductor of the 3H well. When Inflection entered the bore they found a viscous substance in the bore. The substance is suspected to be synthetic oil based drilling fluid. They pumped out the fluid on 9/24/19. According to Inflection, the conductor is cased 80' down with a depth of 100'. The conductor for the 3H well was drilled in February 2017 along with 3 adjacent wells drilled May through September 2017. The 3 adjacent wells were put into production in 2018. The Department investigated around the conductor and there was no apparent staining on the pad or puddles on the pad. The Department then walked the downgrade slope of the pad and noticed a different shade of soil on the edge of the infiltration berm. A soil sample was collected at that site and sent to be analyzed for Oil and Grease and TPH. Lab results are pending. Inflection continues to investigate the source of the fluid. The release of a regulated substance into the Winter 3H conductor is in violation of the Clean Streams Law 402 (b), Chapter 78a.56a, Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. The Department requests Inflection submit a plan of the actions they will take to address the release and to characterize the extent of the pollution in accordance with Chapter 78a.66(c). The Department recommends proceeding in accordance with Act 2 remediation.

Permit API: 015-23838
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/11/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's Crank (03-067) O well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 4/11/2024 at 0900 hours. The weather was 56 degrees F with cloudy skies and light rain. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours as well. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.The site remains set-up for flow back activities. Crews worked today preparing equipment for site removal and recovering fluids within secondary containments and temporary storage tanks. Secondary containment structures remain in working condition with no evidence of leaking observed. The majority of the areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetated cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 570 to 1800us/cm. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed outside of secondary containment. On 3/20/2024, outlined within inspection report #3730668, the DEP observed elevated conductivity fluids pooled on the pad surface field measured at ~5.56mS/cm. Based on the elevated conductivity reading, the DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 (Sample #0983-421). The analytical results from that sample are attached to this inspection report as photos and a file. The findings were reported to Repsol who promptly dispatched an environmental team to collect samples and a water truck to recover the fluid. During today's inspection, the elevated conductivity fluids were determined to have been removed and current fluid in the area was field measured for electrical conductivity at ~890us/cm. Based on the analytical sample results from sample #0983-421 and Repsol's timely response for remediation, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23838:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)The DEP recommends the following:-Recovering the fluid held within the produced water tanks' secondary containment-Recovering the fluid held within the produced water tanks' smaller offload containment-Conducting necessary earth work to return the two smaller leveled surfaces near the entrance to pre-construction conditions and seeding/temporarily stabilizing No additional violations are cited at this time. I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Municipality: Albany Twp

Comments: Weather was 77° and sunny. Met with Chesapeake representative Kevin O'Sullivan on location. Well recently had all casing strings set and cemented. Creston took sample where gas was detected. A 0 to 5k PSI analog pressure gauge was attached to the well head reading approximately 0 PSI. Well is scheduled to be completed in early September.
